Steps.Title: Resolve UI screenshot applicability
Steps.Subtitle: UI routes or no-UI evidence
Steps.Notes: Read the architecture handoff, runtime command nodes, QA evidence, and project structure to decide whether the .NET target has a visible UI. Blazor Server/SSR, Blazor WebAssembly, Blazor WASM PWA, MVC/Razor Pages, SPA-hosted .NET, and other browser surfaces require screenshot capture. Backend-only API/service, worker, console, and class library targets require explicit no-UI evidence. Prefer durable Run app and Run tests node references, but when they are absent and upstream QA/runtime evidence provides a concrete base URL, browser artifact paths, and UI state proving the app is running, continue with a degraded manifest that cites those paths and records missing references as warnings. If no Run app node and no concrete base URL exist but ProductRoot, ProductRootAlias, or DotNetAppProjectDirectory is present, record a launch-required manifest for the capture step instead of claiming degraded runtime evidence is available. Identify the process run node and Screenshots parent target when available; if no writable target is available, require a managed storage receipt instead of blocking during applicability resolution.

Directives.Reason: Applicability planning must not load software-delivery image-analysis guidance before screenshot evidence exists.
Applicability planning is management/review work and suppresses development-only capabilities.

Steps.InputContractSummary: Architecture handoff, runtime command handoff, QA evidence, route nodes, process run node context, and verified upstream browser evidence when command nodes are absent.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Screenshot applicability manifest with UI routes or explicit no-UI evidence.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: App type, UI/no-UI decision, route list, viewport set, runtime command references or degraded runtime evidence, missing-reference warnings, and Screenshots parent target or managed-receipt fallback reason.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Manager may block when UI applicability or route targets are ambiguous.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Block only when UI applicability is contradictory, route targets are empty for a UI app, no concrete launch/browser evidence exists for a UI app, or no-UI evidence is missing for a non-UI target. Missing command nodes or process-run node access are warnings when concrete QA/runtime evidence is available.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind only to a manager-capable operator that can assess screenshot scope.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: .NET UI screenshot target manifest
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by screenshot capture, storage, QA, and release approval.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must include app type, UI/no-UI decision, process run node id when available, Screenshots parent target or managed-receipt fallback reason, base URL or no-UI reason, route list, viewport set, Run app and Run tests node references when available, and exact upstream QA/runtime evidence paths for degraded mode.

Steps.Title: Capture UI screenshots when required
Steps.Subtitle: Current-run browser proof
Steps.Notes: For UI targets, start or reuse the app using the recorded Run app node when available. When the app is not already reachable, call workspace_dotnet_run with targetPath set to DotNetAppProjectFileAlias when present, otherwise DotNetAppProjectFile, with workingDirectory set to ProductRootAlias, WorkspaceAlias, or the equivalent product-root alias, keepAlive enabled, and lifetimeScope set to the current process run. workspace_dotnet_run accepts project files only; never pass DotNetSolutionFile, DotNetSolutionFileAlias, ProductRoot, WorkspaceAlias, DotNetAppProjectDirectory, or any directory path as its targetPath. If a previous attempt used a .sln, .slnx, or directory target, retry once with the app .csproj target before returning Blocked. Missing base URL or missing Run app node is not a successful capture result for a UI target; when those references are missing and DotNetAppProjectFileAlias, DotNetAppProjectFile, ProductRoot, ProductRootAlias, or DotNetAppProjectDirectory is present, call workspace_dotnet_run against the app project file and use the returned current-run URL for browser capture before returning Blocked. workspace_dotnet_run, browser_navigate, browser_snapshot, browser_take_screenshot, browser_console_messages, and workspace_dotnet_stop are declared as required runtime tool receipts for UI targets. If command-node references are missing but the manifest cites verified upstream QA/runtime browser evidence, use the cited base URL as the launch target. Navigate to each concrete route with browser_navigate, capture browser state with browser_snapshot using a durable .yml filename, capture fresh screenshots with browser_take_screenshot using durable .png filenames, collect console messages with browser_console_messages using durable .log filenames, and write screenshot files as current-run managed artifacts. Stop any app process started by this step with workspace_dotnet_stop and include startup and cleanup receipt refs. Do not write Status: Completed, do not say screenshots were captured, and do not hand off to storage until current-run browser_take_screenshot and browser_snapshot receipts exist for each required route and viewport or an explicit no-UI receipt exists. If the capture itself proves the UI is only scaffold chrome, blank, wrong-route, unstyled, non-interactive, or materially inconsistent with a named source visual target, write the screenshot and browser evidence but return Blocked with the concrete visual defect instead of declaring capture complete. Do not return Blocked only because the base URL is absent when a product root or app project file is present; attempt workspace_dotnet_run against the app project file first and cite the receipt. Prior screenshots are source evidence only and must not be submitted as this step output. For no-UI targets, do not launch a browser; write an explicit no-UI screenshot receipt instead. Do not create project-structure nodes or image assets here; the storage step owns Screenshots writeback.

Steps.InputContractSummary: Screenshot target manifest, Run app command node reference when available, or verified upstream runtime URL/browser evidence from the manifest.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Screenshot files and browser evidence for UI targets, or explicit no-UI receipt for non-UI targets.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Current-run browser_take_screenshot files, durable browser_snapshot or browser_evaluate state output, route URLs, browser_console_messages output, runtime command references or cited degraded runtime evidence, workspace_dotnet_run startup receipt, workspace_dotnet_stop cleanup receipt when this step started the app, or no-UI evidence.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Capture agent can block on failed app launch, fatal browser errors, or missing required routes.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not substitute stale screenshots, chat-only claims, or screenshots from another process run.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind only to an agent with runtime and browser screenshot capability.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: .NET UI screenshot files
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by screenshot storage, QA, release, and future layout analysis.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: For UI targets, must include one readable screenshot per required route and viewport. For no-UI targets, must include explicit no-UI receipt and no browser-launch claim.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: .NET UI browser evidence
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by QA and failure triage.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: For UI targets, must include actual URLs, viewport, wait condition, console messages, screenshot paths, runtime command reference or cited degraded runtime evidence, and cleanup receipt. For no-UI targets, must include no-UI rationale.

Steps.Title: Store screenshots under process run node
Steps.Subtitle: Screenshots project-structure parent
Steps.Notes: Create or reuse a Screenshots parent node under the current process run node. Prefer ProcessRunNodeId, ParentProcessRunNodeId, or TargetProcessRunNodeId from launch variables as the parent node id; do not fall back to ProjectNodeId or project root when one of those process-run nodes is present in project structure. For UI targets, inspect each screenshot, reject blank/error/wrong-route images, and create image asset nodes under Screenshots for accepted screenshots. workspace_inspect_image and workspace_analyze_image are declared required runtime tool receipts for this step; call both for every accepted or rejected screenshot and ground the visual reason in the provider-backed result instead of dimensions, filenames, or chat-only descriptions. When project structure, launch variables, the screenshot manifest, or upstream QA evidence list source visual target ImageAsset nodes such as proposals, mockups, reference screenshots, layout targets, or wireframes, resolve the target by node id and media path with project_structure_read, project_structure_asset_get, or project_structure_asset_content_get as needed, then call workspace_analyze_images with the ordered source-target image and delivered screenshot paths when the image files are accessible in the workspace. If the target asset content is not accessible to image-analysis tools, return Blocked with the missing node id, media path, and failed tool receipt instead of accepting screenshots in isolation. The review must include a Visual target comparison section naming the source ImageAsset node id, media path or file name, delivered screenshot ref, comparison method, and accepted or blocked disposition. When accepted UI screenshots exist, project-structure writeback is required and project_structure_node_create plus project_structure_asset_create are declared as required runtime tool receipts for this step: create the missing Screenshots parent with project_structure_node_create using objectType ProjectBlock, objectSubtype delivery, and parentNodeKey set to the process-run node, then call project_structure_asset_create once per accepted screenshot with objectType ImageAsset, objectSubtype screenshot, parentNodeKey set to the Screenshots node, sourceWorkspacePath set to the current-run PNG path, and explicit sourceFileName plus sourceContentType values. Do not infer these tools are unavailable from memory or prompt text; if project_structure_read works, attempt the required writeback tools before reporting a boundary. Do not read binary screenshots as text or base64 when sourceWorkspacePath can be used. If an upload attempt fails because an inline media payload is invalid base64, retry once with sourceWorkspacePath instead of the inline media payload. Do not write Status: Completed, do not say storage completed, and do not hand off with only a managed receipt until project_structure_asset_create has been attempted for every accepted UI screenshot. A managed-only storage receipt is allowed only after the exact project-structure tool call is unavailable, denied, or fails because the process-run/Screenshots parent cannot be read or written; include the failed tool, failed parent target, screenshot path, route, viewport, inspection result, and failure receipt. If project_structure_asset_create or project_structure_node_create is unavailable or denied for this governed step, return Blocked with the missing tool or operation allowance instead of completing silently. For no-UI targets, record a no-UI screenshot receipt under Screenshots or as managed evidence so the parent release step can see that screenshot capture was intentionally not applicable. Do not mutate product files.

Directives.Reason: Screenshot storage reviews interpret generic image evidence through software-delivery acceptance criteria.
Screenshot storage must inspect image metadata before accepting or rejecting screenshots.
Screenshot storage must ground visual screenshot decisions in provider-backed image analysis.
Screenshot storage must compare delivered screenshots with source visual targets when target images exist.

InstructionFragments.Title: Development UI screenshot image analysis
InstructionFragments.Content: Use generic workspace image tools only as software-delivery visual evidence for this step: inspect screenshot readability, route correctness, blank/error states, visible UI behavior, and ordered source-target comparisons against project visual target ImageAssets. Do not treat this as generic image interpretation.

RequiredReceipts.Reason: Screenshot storage must inspect image files before accepting or rejecting them.
Screenshot storage must ground visual decisions in provider-backed image analysis.
Screenshot storage must compare delivered screenshots with source visual targets when target images exist.
Accepted UI screenshots must be stored under a Screenshots parent node when project-structure writeback is available.
Accepted UI screenshots must be written as ImageAsset nodes when project-structure writeback is available.

Steps.InputContractSummary: Screenshot files, browser evidence, and screenshot target manifest.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Screenshots parent node under process run node and image asset storage receipts for accepted screenshots.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Screenshots parent node id and image asset ids from project_structure_node_create and project_structure_asset_create for accepted UI screenshots, or managed storage receipt with explicit failed tool/writeback limitation, plus workspace_inspect_image, workspace_analyze_image, and when source visual targets exist workspace_analyze_images receipt refs, Visual target comparison details, rejected images, and no-UI receipt when applicable.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Storage reviewer can reject unusable screenshots and request recapture instead of storing bad evidence.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Artifact recovery: block when required Screenshots storage receipts are missing, invalid, or not materialized before branch routing. Block when UI screenshots are blank, wrong-route, unreadable, or missing. If project-structure writeback tools are available, do not complete until project_structure_node_create and project_structure_asset_create are attempted and successful for accepted UI screenshots. If project_structure_asset_create or project_structure_node_create is unavailable or denied, return Blocked with the missing tool or operation allowance instead of completing silently.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind only to an agent with image review and project-structure asset write access.
Manager reviews storage receipts and no-UI disposition.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Screenshots project-structure storage receipts
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by parent release approval, project inspection, and later visual review.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must include process run node id and Screenshots parent node id when available, one image asset node id per accepted screenshot when writeback succeeds, or a managed storage receipt with exact writeback limitation, plus route and viewport metadata, sourceWorkspacePath, workspace_inspect_image and workspace_analyze_image receipt refs, rejected screenshot reasons, Visual target comparison details and workspace_analyze_images receipt refs when source visual target ImageAssets exist, and no-UI receipt when applicable.

Steps.Title: Hand off screenshot writeback evidence
Steps.Subtitle: Parent-ready visual proof
Steps.Notes: Summarize screenshot applicability, captured routes, Screenshots parent node id, accepted image asset node ids, rejected images, no-UI evidence, and unresolved blockers for parent release approval. This step writes managed process artifacts only.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Screenshot storage receipts and target manifest.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Applicability, node ids, asset ids, route evidence, no-UI status, and blockers.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Manager may close only when UI targets have stored screenshots or no-UI evidence is explicit.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not close with missing Screenshots storage receipts for UI targets.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Delivery manager owns parent-ready screenshot handoff.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: .NET UI screenshot writeback handoff
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by parent release approval, project structure inspection, and run analysis.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must reference UI/no-UI applicability, process run node id, Screenshots parent node id, accepted image asset node ids, route metadata, storage receipts, rejected screenshots, and unresolved blockers.
